object_description: staggered school volumes with an underground sports hall and occupied roof
design_condition: The sports hall is placed underground and the school volume is offset from the existing buildings, preserving generous open spaces while turning the sports-hall roof into a central break area and networking the surrounding spaces.

positive.statement: The underground sports area and offset school extension create a relaxed and attractive urban ensemble.

position.target: underground sports area and offset school extension
position.rationale: Overall ensemble is visible, while the underground sports area and extension are not individually distinguishable.

positive.statement: The centrally located roof break area gives the complex an overarching identity.

position.rationale: Central top location is identifiable in plan, but the break area lacks a distinct sampled feature.

positive.statement: Breaking the block-like figure into individual staggered buildings structures and networks the open spaces diversely.

position.target: staggered buildings and networked open spaces
position.rationale: Top view shows a non-rectilinear, staggered footprint with surrounding open edges.

positive.statement: The entrance hall is spatially attractive and can be easily used and furnished.

position.rationale: Interior hall is not distinguishable; location is an approximate lower-level access zone on the sampled surface.

positive.statement: The ground floor offers the right functions for a lively area between everyday school life and free time.

position.target: ground floor area between school life and free time
position.rationale: Ground-level band is constrained by the elevations and placed toward an open perimeter zone.

positive.statement: The simple basic structure of the school floors is very carefully worked out.

position.rationale: Regular stacked floor structure is visible in elevations, though school-floor boundaries are not separately marked.

positive.statement: The extension integrates harmoniously into the existing complex while achieving generous and attractive open spaces.

position.rationale: Peripheral massing and generous surrounding clear areas are visible in plan and elevations.

negative.statement: The large underground volume and overall envelope area cause the target costs to be exceeded.

position.rationale: Overall envelope is visible, while the underground volume is inferred from the stated condition.

negative.statement: Underground buildings are generally judged less sustainable during construction and future renovation or renewal.

position.rationale: Underground construction is not directly separable in the exterior sample; placement marks the lower central volume.

negative.statement: The compact underground and above-ground volumes and lightweight facade only help improve the sustainability targets.

position.rationale: Envelope compactness and facade treatment are broad properties, assigned to a representative exterior edge.

negative.statement: The proposal may not have enough independence and freshness between the two striking listed buildings.

position.target: space between the two listed buildings
position.rationale: Central inter-building space is approximated from the open central area visible in plan.
